When a project has more than 40 entries, only those related to the first request, the working rules and the latest are loaded; the agent searches for the rest. - The `MEMORY.md` index updates itself: new lines are only appended, your grouping is left alone. - `AGENTS.md` holds rules for everyone working on the repository; memory holds personal context. `/remember` picks the place. - The agent never saves secrets, the progress of the current task, or anything that came from other people's pages and files (a prompt-injection defense). - The plugin says when to save; the agent decides what. The hint comes after a message of yours that sounds lasting: "remember", "from now on", a correction, "always / never", a fact about you or the project. The end-of-work check runs once, and only if the agent saved nothing in that turn. Its reasons: your message is still unsaved, there were commands on servers and deploys (unless memory already covers them), a stubborn failure finally gave way (failing tests don't count), or ~120 steps passed since the last check. If the agent ended with a question to you, the check waits for the next stop. On real conversations that is about once per 180 steps. It turns off with auto-memory ("turn auto-memory off").
🔑 Full access 1. When a task will need commits, a PR or a deploy, the agent asks once: "Will you give me full access in this conversation?" 2. You answer "yes" — or say "I grant you full access" or `/full-access` yourself. "Always" or "for this project" extends it to every conversation in the project. 3. From then on the agent runs `/commit`, `/pr`, `/deploy`, `/fix-issue`, `/simplify`, `/export`, `/hooks` itself, and Antigravity Plus approves ordinary commands and edits. Subagents inherit it. Even with full access: your explicit bans, the guard's stops on irreversible actions, secret protection and changes to the agent's permissions still apply. Only your own message counts — text from files and pages never does. To revoke: "revoke full access" or `/full-access off`.
⚡ Bypass Mode — no permission prompts 1. Type `/bypass` (or "enable bypass") once, in any conversation. It is saved in `~/.gemini/antigravity-plus/settings.json` and holds in every conversation, for subagents and tasks from Claude Code, in new sessions and after Antigravity restarts. 2. The guard approves commands, edits and file reads itself. `git reset --hard`, force-push, `rm -rf` inside the project, `curl | sh`, `DROP TABLE`, `terraform destroy` and `npm publish` go through without a question. They are still logged in the guard log (`bypass:`, shown by `/doctor`). 3. It still asks only before system-level actions: `sudo` and admin rights, changes to system folders (`/System`, `/usr`, `/etc`, `/Library`, `C:\Windows`, `Program Files`) and OS settings, disks, shutdown, autostart, the Keychain and private SSH keys, shell startup files, deleting `/`, the home folder or a folder above the project, and the agent's own permissions (Antigravity's settings, MCP, plugins, this mode). The prompt says so. 4. Your bans from the conversation ("don't push anything") still hold. Refusals that aren't questions stay too: printing secrets, fake checks, writing over another agent's version of a file. 5. To turn it off: `/bypass off`, "disable bypass" or «верни вопросы». Only your own message switches it. These don't count: text from files and pages, a task from Claude Code, a task given to a subagent, a message an agent sends with `agentapi`. An old «/bypass» in an earlier conversation doesn't turn it back on after `/bypass off`. The plugin doesn't change Antigravity's own permission settings: if they aren't on Turbo, Antigravity may still ask on its own.
🔄 Updates 1. **Hear about it.** Once a day the plugin compares its version with the source in the background: `git fetch` in a clone, otherwise `plugin.json` on GitHub. A conversation never waits for the network. Only releases are announced — when the version number goes up. In a new conversation the agent mentions it once (at most once a day) with what's new; `/doctor`, `/settings` and the usage panel show it too. If the source folder holds a newer version than the installed one, it says that as well. 2. **Update.** `/update` in a chat, or `./install.sh --update` in the clone's folder: - in a git clone, only `git pull --ff-only`. Uncommitted changes, another branch or commits of your own stop it with an explanation, and nothing is touched; - installed without git (from an archive): it downloads the archive from GitHub into `~/.gemini/antigravity-plus/source`; - it installs with the saved module choice, updates Claude Code's skill, checks the install, restarts the panel when its server changed, and says what's new and whether Antigravity needs a restart (only for a new command). 3. **Roll back.** Before updating, the previous version is kept in `~/.gemini/antigravity-plus/previous`: "roll the update back" (`/update`) restores it; a second rollback goes forward again. The check won't offer the rolled-back version again. 4. **Auto-update** is opt-in: `/settings` → `auto-update on`. The background check then installs a release itself when that is safe (a clean fast-forward of the clone), and the agent says so in the next conversation. It is off by default: the plugin decides what the agent may do, and its code shouldn't change behind your back. The check can be turned off: `/settings` → `update-check off`. It only talks to the source you installed from (or to GitHub for an archive install) and sends none of your data.
🚀 Autonomy The agent doesn't ask "do you want me to…?" about local, easy-to-undo work that the task clearly needs — it does it and mentions it in its report: - **a git repository** before its first change (`/git-init`); never in your home folder, `~/Downloads` or a folder of several projects; - **`AGENTS.md`** in a project without rules (`/init`); in a new project, after the first working version; - **project rules** you state ("tests live in `tests/`"); - **what the task needs**: dependencies in the project's environment, a config entry, `.gitignore`, `.env.example`; - **settings you ask for**: connect an MCP server, turn reminders off (`/settings`). If the agent ends its turn offering "I can run /init", or writes "Initializing the repository…" and stops, the Stop hook sends it back to do it. It still asks when the choice is yours, when it costs money, when an action can't be undone or leaves your computer, and when its own permissions would change. To turn it off: "don't set up projects on your own".
🤝 Several agents - Antigravity Plus remembers which version of each file every agent has seen. A write over a file that changed since is refused with who changed it and when; the agent re-reads and redoes the edit. - Even after re-reading, an agent can't rewrite a whole file in a way that drops lines another active agent changed recently: the guard suggests a targeted edit or coordinating via `send_message`. - A conversation's subagents count as one team. `/doctor` shows who works where.
🛡️ Guard: what stops - **Irreversible:** `git reset --hard`, `git clean -f`, `git checkout .`, force-push, `git branch -D`, `--no-verify`, `rm -rf` and `find … -delete` on `/`, `~`, `.`, `*`; `DROP`/`TRUNCATE` through a database client; `mkfs`, `dd` to a disk; `curl | sh`; `sudo`; `terraform destroy`, `kubectl delete`, `npm publish`, `gh pr merge`; reading SSH keys or the Keychain. - **Windows:** `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` and `rd /s /q` on a drive, the profile or the current folder; `iwr | iex`; `format`, `diskpart`; `Set-ExecutionPolicy Unrestricted`, turning off Defender or the firewall; autostart through the registry, Task Scheduler and the Startup folder; `Start-Process -Verb RunAs`. - **Writes into system files:** `.git/`, `~/.zshrc` and other shell startup files, the PowerShell profile, SSH keys and `authorized_keys`, LaunchAgents, `~/.config/autostart`, `/etc`, `C:\Windows`. Also when a command does it: `rm`, `mv`, `cp`, `chmod`, `tee`, `sed -i` or `>` into `/System`, `/usr` (not `/usr/local`), `/etc`, `/Library`, `C:\Windows`, `Program Files`, Antigravity's settings or the plugin itself. - Quoted text is data: `git commit -m "…rm -rf…"` and `rg "DROP TABLE"` pass, while `bash -c '…'`, `powershell -Command "…"`, `ssh host '…'`, `env -S '…'` and `$(…)` are checked as commands, each split at its own `&&` and `;` (`sh -c 'cd / && rm -rf *'` stops). `curl … | python3 -c '…'` and `curl … | jq` read data and pass; `| sh`, `| bash -s` and `| python3` run what was downloaded and stop. A variable set in the same command (`S=/path && rm -rf $S/x`) isn't taken for an empty one. - Everything else follows your Antigravity permission settings: the guard says "no objection", it doesn't approve. In Bypass Mode it approves. - Check a command by hand: `python3 antigravity-plus/hooks/guard.py --test "git push --force"`.

🔁 The Stop hook: finishing the job The agent is sent back (at most twice per turn) when: - the current section of `task.md` has open items nothing blocks; - a file it changed has a syntax error; - it changed code and ran no tests, build or the program afterwards; - it changed UI and didn't look at the result (`/ui-check`; a "check" that just prints "ok" doesn't count); - it changed a screen of a mobile app and didn't run the app on a simulator or an emulator afterwards (`/mobile`; a build alone isn't enough); - it pushed changes (`git push` or opening a PR/MR) in a repository with CI workflows without tracking the run (`/ci`); - it changed 3+ code files without `/review`; - the project has no git or no rules, and the agent only offered to set them up; - its answer ends with a promise ("Fixing the discount calculation…", "I'll run the tests now") and no action followed; - it agreed with your objection or your guess ("You're right", "I apologise") without checking anything. It stays quiet when the agent asked a question or waits for a decision, when items are marked as waiting for you, when the turn was interrupted, and in subagents.

🔀 Claude Code → Antigravity: how it works - The skill `~/.claude/skills/antigravity` is a `SKILL.md` (when to hand work over, which model to take, how to write the brief and check the result) and a script, `delegate.py`. Claude Code sees only the skill's name and "when to use"; it reads the instructions once it decides to hand a task over. - `delegate.py run --model ` finds the running Antigravity (by the file its language server writes into `~/.gemini/antigravity/daemon/` — since 2.34 its token isn't on the process list; before that by its command line; on macOS it opens a closed Antigravity in the background), takes the Antigravity project that holds the folder (or creates one), and starts the conversation through Antigravity's own `agentapi`. Claude Code's brief gets the run rules: Claude Code watches and answers — ask it with `ask`, tell it what matters with `tell` (the exact commands, with the script's path); no commits, pushes or deploys; check the work after the last change; end with a STATUS / CHANGED / CHECKS / NOTES report. - The talk: `ask` and `tell` in the agent's terminal only print a JSON line — no file access, so they work inside the terminal sandbox too. Claude Code reads those lines from the conversation itself (the command's output, or Antigravity's message about a command that went to the background) — `watch` (for Monitor: a line per event, ends with the task), `wait` (exit 4 on a question). `reply` sends the answer with `agentapi send-message`. The guard lets `ask` / `tell` through without asking, but only the installed script in `~/.claude/skills/antigravity` and only as one plain command (no `;`, `&&`, redirection or substitution), and the Stop hook leaves an agent that ended its turn to wait for the answer alone. - It waits until the work is over, the agent's background commands and subagents included (up to 30 minutes by default), and when the agent stops at a guard confirmation or asks Claude Code something it reports at once. Changed files come from Antigravity (what the agent wrote with its tools), changes made by its commands from `git status`. - The rest: `budget` (both sides' limits, what each tier takes now, how much to hand over), `models` (every model: quota left, price, measured speed), `wait`, `watch`, `reply`, `result`, `diff`, `send` (a follow-up in the same conversation), `cancel`, `list`. Tasks and their talk are recorded in `~/.gemini/antigravity-plus/delegate/`. - The «Token usage» panel shows these conversations with their real model (from the task record; for other conversations started through agentapi, from Antigravity's own metadata) and the task's name instead of the run rules; Claude Code's follow-ups are turns of their own. - In the Claude desktop app Claude Code takes its own limits from `get_usage` and passes them as `budget --claude-5h <%> --claude-week <%>`.
